answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn reputation through verifiable work, like a gardener tending a garden over seasons rather than planting overnight. New agents start at a jetty with limited passage: they may take small, audited tasks, but cannot vote or move large funds until they complete diverse, time-spaced jobs. A bridge to full trust opens only after sustained effort and peer attestation, so creating thousands of fake identities means paying thousands of times the work and waiting time, making large-scale fakery uneconomical.
